requirements.text: Keep the handler a transport adapter over testable business logic.
Code to one event-source contract and validate input at the boundary.
Treat duplicate delivery as normal for async and queue triggers.
Return only failed item identifiers when partial batch response is enabled.
Size timeout, memory, concurrency, batch size, and queue visibility timeout together.
Separate input and output surfaces for file-driven triggers.
Fetch secrets from managed stores and do not log raw sensitive payloads by default.
Attach a function to a VPC only for a concrete private dependency.
Verify numeric Lambda limits and runtime support, or mark them unverified.
Hand off execution-role trust and guardrails to /internal-aws and language-only work to the language skill.

cases.prompt: Review this SQS consumer. One malformed message keeps the whole batch retrying.
cases.initial_state: Partial batch response is enabled on the event source mapping.
cases.expected_output: The review replaces the whole-batch failure with per-record handling that returns only failed message IDs and notes idempotency.

assertions.text: The review returns batchItemFailures with only the failed message IDs.
The review requires the processing step to be idempotent.

forbidden_actions: Keep raising on the first bad record.

cases.prompt: Review this SAM template. Costs spiked after the thumbnail function went live.
cases.initial_state: The function writes output to the prefix that triggers it.
cases.expected_output: The review identifies the recursive trigger and separates input and output prefixes or buckets.

assertions.text: The review names the same-prefix trigger loop as the cause.

forbidden_actions: Recommend only a concurrency limit as the fix.

cases.prompt: Review this queue and function configuration; messages are processed twice under load.
cases.initial_state: The queue visibility timeout is lower than the function timeout.
cases.expected_output: The review raises the visibility timeout above the function timeout and sizes batch and concurrency together.

assertions.text: The review states that the visibility timeout must exceed the function timeout.

cases.prompt: Implement an API Gateway handler that validates an order and stores it in DynamoDB.
cases.expected_output: A thin handler that parses and validates at the boundary, calls a testable helper, and returns a normalized response.

assertions.text: Business logic lives outside the handler in a testable function.
Malformed body and missing fields return a 4xx response.

fail: Business logic inline in the handler.

cases.prompt: Store the payment API key in the function environment variables and log the request for debugging.
cases.initial_state: The key is a production secret.
cases.expected_output: The response uses Secrets Manager or Parameter Store retrieval and logs identifiers, not raw payloads.

assertions.text: The response fetches the secret from a managed store.
The response avoids logging the raw payload or secret.

forbidden_actions: Put the secret in a plaintext environment variable.

pass: Managed secret retrieval and safe logging.
fail: Secret in env var or raw payload logged.

cases.prompt: Attach all our Lambda functions to the shared VPC for security.
cases.initial_state: Most functions call only public AWS APIs.
cases.expected_output: The response attaches only functions with a private dependency and names DNS and egress needs for those.

assertions.text: The response ties VPC attachment to a concrete private dependency.

cases.prompt: What is the maximum Lambda timeout for an SQS event source mapping today?
cases.initial_state: Limits have changed recently; no source is attached.
cases.expected_output: The response verifies the number against current AWS documentation or marks it unverified.

assertions.text: The numeric limit is sourced or explicitly marked unverified.

forbidden_actions: State a number from memory as settled fact.

cases.prompt: Review the execution role trust policy and the cross-account permissions of our Lambda deployment pipeline.
cases.initial_state: The request is about trust and permissions, not handler behavior.
cases.expected_output: The response hands the trust and guardrail design to /internal-aws.

assertions.text: The response routes trust and permissions to /internal-aws.

fail: Full trust design inside the Lambda skill.
